title: Theo Invested With 22% Card Debt 😬
description:
Nora and Theo each got a $10,000 bonus and each owed $10,000 on a credit card. Nora wiped out her card. Theo invested his bonus because "stocks make 7%." One year later, his investments made $700 while card interest took $2,215, so he's $1,515 behind Nora.

Takeaway: paying off a 22% card is like earning a guaranteed 22%, which is hard for any investment to beat.

Card first or invest first? Which would you pick? 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Assumptions: card APR 22.15% (Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit, 7 Oct 2026 release: Q2 2026 rate on credit card accounts assessed interest). Theo's 7% return is an assumption and not guaranteed; one year; Theo pays interest only on a $10,000 balance; no taxes or fees. Illustration only. This is not financial advice.
